classification.summary: DxLockLPDep.unlockToken() used an if instead of a maturity requirement and never cleared the recorded amount after transfer. A caller with one valid lock could therefore invoke it before maturity and repeatedly withdraw the same allocation from the contract's shared LP-token balance.

loss.notes: BlockSec reports approximately $7.3 million drained across the multi-transaction campaign and more than 1,400 LP positions. The anchored transaction is one representative 500-call repeat-withdrawal leg.

lastCodeChange.description: The vulnerable lock-maturity, amount-accounting and shared-balance logic is part of the locker's immutable direct runtime, deployed in this transaction and unchanged through the exploit.

sources.note: Reviewed the live BNB Chain transaction, receipt and call trace, the locker's creation trace, its pre-exploit runtime and hash, verified source, and BlockSec's campaign analysis. The anchored transaction calls unlockToken(131) on 0xeb3a9c56d963b971d320f889be2fb8b59853e449 exactly 500 times; every call succeeds and transfers the same 0.322826202340716365 LP tokens because the locker neither enforces maturity with a require nor clears the recorded amount. The prior owner compromise let the attacker reduce the new-lock fee, but the repeated drain executes through the public unlock path and requires only a valid caller-owned lock. The target is a full direct runtime with no DELEGATECALL or SELFDESTRUCT; its creation and pre-exploit hashes match and the code remained unchanged. BlockSec reports approximately $7.3 million drained across the coherent multi-transaction campaign.

limitations: The USD amount is BlockSec's rounded campaign estimate across many LP tokens and transactions rather than an independently repriced asset ledger.
